title: What to Watch This Week: Seven Streams Worth Your Weekend
excerpt: From Akshay Kumar's haunted palace to Suriya playing God, from a 1978 Delhi kidnapping to the Michael Jackson biopic — your streaming guide for June 8-14.
body:
The streaming gods are feeling generous this week. Between blockbusters making their digital debuts, a true-crime series that's already being called the year's best, and a Michael Jackson biopic starring an actual Jackson — there's enough here to cancel every plan you had through Sunday. Here are seven picks, ranked by how likely they are to ruin your sleep schedule.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=RdB_TgwLPqs</youtube>

## 1. Raakh — Prime Video

**The one that'll haunt you.**

Let's start with the show everyone will be talking about by Monday. **Ali Fazal** plays a rookie sub-inspector in 1978 Delhi, hunting two kidnappers who've taken a pair of teenage siblings. The series is loosely based on the infamous **Ranga-Billa case** — a crime so brutal it changed Indian law enforcement forever.

But *Raakh* isn't just a procedural. Director **Prosit Roy** builds it like a horror film that happens to involve police work. **Akash Makhija** and **Ramandeep Yadav** as the two killers deliver performances so unsettling that reviewers are calling them the breakout acts of the year. **Sonali Bendre**, in her first major role in years, plays the mother — and the grief she carries is devastating enough to make you forget she was ever in *Hum Saath-Saath Hain*.

Critics are giving it 3.5 to 4.5 stars across the board. India Forums called it "the year's best show." They're not wrong.

> "Raakh is gripping, disturbing, and deeply immersive. Every episode steadily builds tension, making the mystery more intense while maintaining a strong emotional connection with the family at the center." — Kuldeep Gadhvi

**Where to watch:** Amazon Prime Video (available in US, UK, Canada, India)

## 2. Bhooth Bangla — Netflix

**The one for the whole family. Sort of.**

**Akshay Kumar** and **Priyadarshan** together again. If you grew up on *Hera Pheri* and *Bhool Bhulaiyaa*, that sentence alone is enough. The premise: Akshay's character inherits an ancestral palace in rural Mangalpur, decides to host his sister's wedding there, and discovers — surprise — the place is extremely haunted.

After a ₹264 crore theatrical run, the horror-comedy arrives on Netflix with **Tabu**, **Paresh Rawal**, and **Wamiqa Gabbi** in a cast that knows exactly what kind of film they're in. Priyadarshan's comic timing hasn't lost a step. The scares are fun, the comedy is broad, and the production design of the crumbling palace is genuinely gorgeous.

Perfect popcorn energy. Watch it loud.

**Where to watch:** Netflix (global)

## 3. Karuppu — Prime Video

**The one where Suriya plays a deity. And it works.**

**Suriya**'s Tamil fantasy blockbuster finally hits streaming after a ₹300 crore theatrical rampage. The setup is deceptively simple: a father loses his savings meant for his daughter's liver transplant to thugs. The courts fail him. The system fails him. So he prays to the guardian deity Vettai Karuppu — who descends to Earth as a fearless lawyer.

Yes, it's part courtroom drama, part divine intervention, part action spectacle. **Trisha Krishnan** and **RJ Balaji** round out a cast that takes a wild premise and commits to it completely. If you haven't been following Tamil cinema's current hot streak, this is your entry point.

**Where to watch:** Amazon Prime Video (Hindi dub available for non-Tamil speakers in the diaspora)

## 4. Michael — Prime Video / Apple TV+

**The one everyone has an opinion about before watching.**

The **Michael Jackson** biopic has arrived, and yes, that's **Jaafar Jackson** — Michael's actual nephew — playing the King of Pop. The film covers Michael's journey from the Jackson 5 childhood through the late '80s megastardom, with **Colman Domingo** anchoring the emotional weight as Joe Jackson.

Director Antoine Fuqua and screenwriter John Logan (*Gladiator*, *The Aviator*) keep the focus on the music and the family dynamics. Whether the film fully reckons with Jackson's complicated legacy is debatable, but the performance sequences are electrifying, and Jaafar's physical resemblance is genuinely eerie.

Available for rental — worth it for the concert recreations alone.

**Where to watch:** Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+ (rental)

## 5. Dridam — JioHotstar

**The one for Malayalam cinema converts.**

**Shane Nigam** plays a newly appointed sub-inspector posted to Kuzhinilam, a seemingly sleepy village in Idukki, Kerala. When human remains are discovered, he has a week to solve the case. Director Martin Joseph builds the tension methodically — this is less *Drishyam* fireworks and more slow-burn atmosphere, where the hills themselves feel like they're hiding something.

Malayalam cinema continues to operate on a different plane. If you've been meaning to explore beyond Bollywood, Dridam is a clean 2.5-hour entry point with no franchise homework required.

**Where to watch:** JioHotstar

## 6. Sweet Magnolias Season 5 — Netflix

**The one your mom will love. And honestly, you might too.**

The Serenity gang is back. If you've been following **Maddie**, **Dana Sue**, and **Helen** through four seasons of Southern charm, romantic complications, and enough sweet tea to fill a swimming pool, Season 5 picks up right where the last cliffhanger left off. It's comfort viewing at its most reliable — warm, well-acted, and paced for a weekend binge.

For diaspora viewers: if you've ever tried to explain the concept of a small-town American drama to your parents and failed, just put this on. They'll be hooked by episode two.

**Where to watch:** Netflix (global)

## 7. Shelter — Lionsgate Play

**The one where Statham does Statham things.**

**Jason Statham** plays a retired operative living on a remote island who gets pulled back in when his orphaned niece is endangered after a violent storm. **Bill Nighy** shows up. **Naomi Ackie** shows up. Things explode. People get punched through walls.

You know exactly what you're getting, and sometimes that's exactly what a Friday night needs. Lean, efficient, 100 minutes of a very competent man being very competent at violence.

**Where to watch:** Lionsgate Play

|-------|----------|-------|----------------|
| **Raakh** | Prime Video | Crime thriller | ★★★ Must-watch |
| **Bhooth Bangla** | Netflix | Horror-comedy | ★★★ Family night |
| **Karuppu** | Prime Video | Fantasy action | ★★★ Tamil blockbuster |
| **Michael** | Prime/Apple (rental) | Biopic | ★★ Music fans |
| **Dridam** | JioHotstar | Crime thriller | ★★ Malayalam gem |
| **Sweet Magnolias S5** | Netflix | Drama | ★★ Comfort binge |
| **Shelter** | Lionsgate Play | Action | ★ Popcorn night |

**The move this weekend:** Start with *Raakh* on Friday night. Decompress with *Bhooth Bangla* on Saturday. Save *Karuppu* for Sunday when you want spectacle without subtlety. You're welcome.
